title: resolveFinalPath infinite-loops on a recorded rename cycle (mv a b; mv b a)
description: DEFER UNTIL AFTER THE LAYER 1 VIEW MILESTONE (spec S18, tasks #230-#239) IS COMPLETE. Task-203 finding (2026-07-25): while building the layered lineage walk, resolveFinalPath (src/reconstruction_lineage.ts) was found to follow the rename chain without a seen-set, so a transcript that records `mv a b` followed by `mv b a` — which real sessions do produce when a rename is undone — makes it loop forever rather than terminating on the cycle. The new layered walk in jfred/src/layered_lineage.ts avoids this by carrying a shared seen-set across both directions, and the engine's version was deliberately left untouched so the fix could be scoped and verified on its own. Add a seen-set (or an explicit cycle error) to resolveFinalPath and every other rename-chain walker that shares the pattern, with a unit test that records the two-hop cycle and asserts termination. No live scenario is known to trigger it yet, so a synthetic fixture is acceptable evidence.

title: renderRevisionText unconditionally appends a trailing newline, so files without one can never blob-match
description: DEFER UNTIL AFTER THE LAYER 1 VIEW MILESTONE (spec S18, tasks #230-#239) IS COMPLETE. Task-187 finding (2026-07-25): renderRevisionText renders a revision as linesTextOf(rev).join("\n") + "\n" — the trailing newline is unconditional. A file whose real bytes do NOT end in a newline therefore can never hash-match its recorded blob. In the 68-file M sweep this produced a 2/2 correlation: exactly 2 of the 68 baseline blobs lack a trailing newline (docs/design/architecture.md ending 0x2e, docs/design/milestones.md ending 0x2e) and those are exactly the 2 baselineBlobMatched=false rows. The same artifact also corrupts the diskMatched comparison for 3 further files. Fixing this means the engine must carry a 'final line had no newline' bit, which touches the LineEntry vocabulary and every producer/consumer of it — CONFIRM the design with the user before implementing (open question 2 in plans/implementation-notes-tasks-223-224-184-203-207-187.md). Evidence: plans/166-per-file-target.md, section "Task 187 — the M-file sweep (68 files)".

title: Extend the task-224 seed clamp to the two sibling backup stampers (needs a reproducer first)
description: DEFER UNTIL AFTER THE LAYER 1 VIEW MILESTONE (spec S18, tasks #230-#239) IS COMPLETE. Task-224 follow-up (2026-07-25): task 224 fixed the non-monotonic ladder by giving backup-sourced seeds a two-sided placement window via clampSeedBetweenPreviousAndEdit (jfred/src/reconstruction_sidecar.ts), but wired it into ONE proven site — seedStaleEditBases in jfred/src/reconstruction_reseed.ts. Two sibling stampers apply the identical `timestamp: <backupTime>` pattern and therefore share the defect CLASS: backupAfterWriteFor (reconstruction_sidecar.ts:90-96, used by reversedEditBaseSeed at reconstruction_reseed.ts:157) and backupWritesFor (reconstruction_sidecar.ts:116-122, used at reconstruction_beacons.ts:158 and via latestBackupWriteFor at reconstruction_beacons.ts:56). They were deliberately NOT changed: completeElidedBeacons and completeTruncatedBeacon are load-bearing for many character-locked scenarios (S27, S28, S30 among others) and already carry their own retiming logic — completeElidedBeacons re-times the BEACON backward when its seed precedes it — so extending the clamp without a reproducer risks breaking locked ground truths to fix a defect nobody has observed. REQUIRE a reproducing scenario that shows one of these two stampers emitting an out-of-order seed BEFORE changing them; then reuse the existing clamp and run the full suite.

title: Layer 1 View: clicking a ruler row does not jump to the first bubble with that timestamp
description: Layer 1 View bug (user report 2026-07-26, voice). In the user's words: "clicking a ruler row does not jump to the first bubble with that same time stamp." This is the task #260 feature failing in practice against the live render, despite passing its 3 unit tests. The implementation is jfred/webapp/layer1-ruler-click.ts: `findBubbleForAxisPx` runs a two-stage lookup — stage 1 matches a `.filebox` whose own `--axis-px` equals the clicked tick's offset (a bubble that BEGINS at that instant), stage 2 falls back to `bubbleAxisPx + nodeAxisPx` for a bubble merely holding a node there. Re-verify against the REAL render, not the fixture: likely suspects are that the equality comparison never matches because the values are floats after task #251's content-driven spacing, or that the handler is attached to a tick element that is replaced on re-render. Note task #268 may merge duplicate ruler rows, which changes which tick is clickable.

Reuse that convention.

title: Layer 1 View: merge ruler rows that display the same time value into a single row
description: Layer 1 View fix (user report 2026-07-26, voice). In the user's words: "there are many ruler rows that have the same time value. if the ruler row is showing milliseconds, then rows with the same value should all be combined into one row." TODAY: `formatInstantLabel` in jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts renders "MM-DD HH:MM" (no seconds, no milliseconds), and `renderRulerTicks` drops a label only when it would PHYSICALLY collide with the one above it (TICK_LABEL_MIN_GAP_PX = 13). So distinct instants that render to the same visible text still occupy separate rows whenever they are far enough apart in pixels, and the gutter reads as a run of identical timestamps. Decide with care whether the merge happens on the DISPLAYED string or on the underlying instant, and at what precision — the user's phrasing ties it to what the label shows. Changing the number of ruler entries affects task #264 (one leader per entry) and task #266 (which tick is clickable).

title: Layer 1 View: bubble file names are truncated and should be readable
description: Layer 1 View visual issue (user report 2026-07-26, voice). In the user's words: "bubble file names are truncated." Since task #245 the `.fname` label shows the BASENAME only, with the full path in the element's `title` attribute, and the `.fname` rule in jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css bounds it with `max-width: calc(100% - 24px); overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis` so a long name cannot overprint neighbouring bubbles. The bubble is a fixed 168 px wide, so any basename longer than roughly 20 characters still ellipsises — visible in the user's screenshot as several bubbles reading `971e94bac3cb2811...`. The user wants the names READABLE. Decide the mechanism (wider or variable-width bubbles, wrapping onto a second line, a smaller font for long names, or something else) — do not simply remove the max-width, which reinstates the #245 overprinting bug.

title: Layer 1 View: show the event count in parentheses to the right of each ruler row
description: Layer 1 View feature (user request 2026-07-26, voice). In the user's own words: "it would be useful to have the number of events in parentheses shown to the right of each timeline ruler row: ex: 07-18 19:42:08.22 (6). this means there are six events that occurred at that timestamp." So a ruler row reads `<timestamp> (<n>)` where n is how many events share that instant. The ruler is rendered by renderRulerTicks in jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts from the `ruler` array returned by /api/layer1-view (jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1.ts); that array currently carries only `{ instant, axisPx }` per entry, so the COUNT has to be derived — either added to the wire by the endpoint (which already knows every pair's node ladder, and since task #251 already computes per-instant row demand in src/layer1_ruler_axis.ts) or counted on the page. Prefer the endpoint: the page deliberately does no arithmetic over the wire data. Pairs naturally with task #268 (merging rows that show the same value) and task #276 (showing seconds and milliseconds).

title: Layer 1 View: the ruler should show seconds and milliseconds, not just month/day and hours/minutes
description: Layer 1 View fix (user report 2026-07-26, voice). In the user's own words: "the ruler should show more of the timestamp information. the ruler appears to only show month/day + hours and minutes, not seconds or milliseconds." Confirmed: `formatInstantLabel` in jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts is `new Date(instant).toISOString().slice(5, 16).replace('T', ' ')`, which yields exactly "MM-DD HH:MM" and discards seconds and milliseconds. Because of that truncation, instants that are seconds apart render as identical text, which is the direct cause of the duplicate-looking rows in task #268 — the user's phrasing there ("if the ruler row is showing milliseconds, then rows with the same value should all be combined") assumes THIS task lands first. Widen the label to include seconds and milliseconds (the example given in task #275 is `07-18 19:42:08.22`); note the `.ruler .tick` rule in jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css currently allots the label a fixed 70 px against an 80 px gutter, so the gutter will need to grow with the longer text.

title: Layer 1 View: make the File Nav column resizable by dragging its right edge
description: User request 2026-07-26, in their own wording: "the file nav column should be resizable. right edge of the column should be draggable to resize." The pane landed in task 252 as `<aside class=\"filenav\">` inside `.stagewrap` in jfred/webapp/layer1.html, styled in jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css with a hardcoded `width: 232px`. TRAP: `.minimap` is `position: absolute` against `.stagewrap`, and task 252 set its `left` to `calc(232px + 12px)` to clear the pane — that literal REPEATS the pane's width, so whatever makes the width dynamic must drive the minimap's `left` from the same value or the minimap will drift over the pane (or back over the ruler) as the user drags. Native-first options to weigh before writing a drag handler: CSS `resize: horizontal` on `.filenav` costs zero JS but puts the grabber in the bottom-right corner rather than along the whole right edge as asked, and cannot update the minimap; a small pointerdown/pointermove handler writing ONE custom property (e.g. `--filenav-w` on `.viz-root`) that BOTH `.filenav`'s width and `.minimap`'s `left` read is the smallest thing that satisfies the request as worded and removes the duplicated literal at the same time. Note task 269 (minimap overlapping the ruler) touches the same `.minimap` positioning and should be settled first or together.

title: Layer 1 View: hovering a truncated bubble file name must reveal the full name in-page, not as a native tooltip
description: User clarification 2026-07-26, in their own wording: "there's a task that says file names in bubbles are truncated. for that task, when you mouse over the file name in the bubble the full file name should be shown. right now the full file name appears as a tool tip." This REFINES existing task 270 ("Layer 1 View: bubble file names are truncated and should be readable") rather than replacing it: 270 covers making the name readable at all, this pins the specific hover behaviour asked for. CURRENT STATE: jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts's buildPairWidget renders `el(\"div\", { class: \"fname\", text: basename, title: pair.path })`, so the full path is reachable ONLY through the native `title` tooltip — which the user is explicitly rejecting (slow to appear, unstyled, vanishes on movement). `.filebox .fname` in jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css is `position: absolute` with `max-width: calc(100% - 24px)`, `overflow: hidden`, `text-overflow: ellipsis`, `white-space: nowrap`; that ellipsis is the truncation. FIX DIRECTION: on `:hover`, let the name escape the bubble's width so the full path is revealed in-page immediately — CSS-only, no JS. TRAP: the neighbouring bubbles sit only 26 px apart in `.stage` (the `.stage` gap), so a revealed long name will paint over them unless it also gets an opaque background and a z-index above its siblings. Task 270 should be settled with this one, not separately — they are the same widget's name.

title: Layer 1 View: global toggle to place bubbles by author vs committer timestamp
description: User request 2026-07-26, in their own wording: "add a global toggle next to the zoom buttons to place bubbles on the timeline using 'author' timestamps or committer timestamps. the 'CommitTouch' interface (/Users/matkatmusicllc/Desktop/claude code src/RevEng/jfred/src/layered_git_beacons.ts) will need 'authorEpochSeconds: number'. Line 31 'listCommitsTouchingFile' will need an optional arg (authorOrCommitter: boolean) to decide how git should be spawned (line 32) to get the author/committer timestamp." WHY THIS IS REAL, NOT HYPOTHETICAL: on 2026-07-26 the user saw two commits wrapped by task 259's same-instant rectangle whose git-GUI dates were days apart — specs/bug screenshots/'git commit timestamps computed wrong.png'. Verified against this repo: fc5ad81 and e677bd9 BOTH carry `%ct 1783459471` (2026-07-07T14:24:31-07:00) while their AUTHOR dates are Jul 4 and Jul 5.
